title: Rational Weil descent of a unit-compatible integral tensor comparison
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $q=p^a$ with $a\ge1$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite intermediate field $E\subset\Omega$, with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $W_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $W=W_0\times_{k_0}k$, and $B=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(R/\varpi^n)_W$ on the small pro-etale site. Use the integral bounded-constructible category $\mathcal C_E$ underlying [def-wf-weil-category].
Let $H=\Phi_W^*$ be geometric-Frobenius coefficient transport [def-wf-weil-category]. Suppose the ordinary tensor $T_E(M,N)=M\otimes_B^L N$ and completed tensor $\widehat T_E(M,N)=C(T_E(M,N))$ [def-wf-tensor-product] are bifunctors on $\mathcal C_E$ with their prescribed pullback comparisons $\mu_E^{\mathrm{ord}}$ and $\widehat\mu_E$. Suppose the actual completion-unit components $\chi_{M,N}=\eta_{T_E(M,N)}$ form a natural isomorphism and satisfy
$$\widehat\mu_E\circ H(\chi_{M,N})=\chi_{HM,HN}\circ\mu_E^{\mathrm{ord}}.$$
Use raw rationalization $\mathcal C_E[1/\varpi]$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], keeping objects and localizing Hom modules, with the prescribed tensor action $(u/\varpi^r,v/\varpi^s)\mapsto T_E(u,v)/\varpi^{r+s}$, and likewise for $\widehat T_E$. The localized $\chi$ is natural on all rational arrows. For arbitrary rational Weil isomorphisms $\varphi_M:HM\to M$, $\varphi_N:HN\to N$ it satisfies
$$\chi_{M,N}\circ T_E(\varphi_M,\varphi_N)\circ\mu_E^{\mathrm{ord}}
=\widehat T_E(\varphi_M,\varphi_N)\circ\widehat\mu_E\circ H(\chi_{M,N}).$$
Consequently $\chi$ and $\chi^{-1}$ are inverse morphisms of the corresponding rational Weil pairs. Integral numerators representing the rational Weil isomorphisms are not required to be integral isomorphisms.
If the stated integral hypotheses hold at every finite intermediate field, let input Weil objects be given at finite fields $E,F\subset\Omega$, and let $L\subset\Omega$ be any finite field containing both. Apply the transition functors $T_{L/E},T_{L/F}$ of [def-wf-weil-category]. The comparison on these two objects at $L$, and its inverse, give inverse common-stage Weil morphisms $[L,\chi]$, $[L,\chi^{-1}]$ between the ordinary and completed tensor objects represented at $L$. This conclusion includes $L=E=F$ and makes no assertion equating comparison components at different fields without the transition identifications.

proof.text: Write $Q$ for raw rationalization and suppress $Q$ on components. By [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], $Q$ preserves composition and identities. Thus $Q(\chi_{M,N})Q(\chi_{M,N}^{-1})=1$ and $Q(\chi_{M,N}^{-1})Q(\chi_{M,N})=1$; the localized components are isomorphisms.

source.place: Penultimate sentence, equivariance for Weil complexes; argument extracted from lem-wf-tensor-completion-frobenius, original step 5; raw rationalization and common-stage Weil morphisms

proof.text: Let $u:M\to M'$, $v:N\to N'$ be integral arrows. Integral naturality gives $\chi_{M',N'}T_E(u,v)=\widehat T_E(u,v)\chi_{M,N}$. For $f=u/\varpi^r$, $g=v/\varpi^s$, divide this equality in the localized Hom module by $\varpi^{r+s}$. The prescribed tensor actions give $\chi_{M',N'}T_E(f,g)=\widehat T_E(f,g)\chi_{M,N}$. This covers all arrows: each element of $\operatorname{Hom}\otimes_R E$ is a finite sum of pure tensors; each scalar has a power-of-$\varpi$ denominator, and a common denominator puts the sum in the displayed form. No cancellation in an integral Hom module is used.

source.place: Penultimate sentence, equivariance for Weil complexes; argument extracted from lem-wf-tensor-completion-frobenius, original step 5; raw rationalization and common-stage Weil morphisms

proof.text: Apply $Q$ to the assumed integral compatibility. Since Frobenius on the rational category is the rationalization of integral coefficient transport [def-wf-weil-category], this reads $\widehat\mu_E H(\chi_{M,N})=\chi_{HM,HN}\mu_E^{\mathrm{ord}}$ in the rational category. This step only sends a given equality through a functor.

proof.text: Apply Step 2 with $f=\varphi_M:HM\to M$ and $g=\varphi_N:HN\to N$, then compose on the right with $\mu_E^{\mathrm{ord}}$. Substitution from Step 3 gives $\chi_{M,N}T_E(\varphi_M,\varphi_N)\mu_E^{\mathrm{ord}}=\widehat T_E(\varphi_M,\varphi_N)\widehat\mu_E H(\chi_{M,N})$. The two tensor Frobenius maps are precisely these composites [def-wf-tensor-product]. Step 2 used arbitrary numerators, so their integral invertibility was never needed.

source.place: Penultimate sentence, equivariance for Weil complexes; argument extracted from lem-wf-tensor-completion-frobenius, original step 5; raw rationalization and common-stage Weil morphisms

proof.text: Put $A=T_E(M,N)$, $D=\widehat T_E(M,N)$, with tensor Weil maps $\alpha,\delta$. Step 4 is $\chi\alpha=\delta H(\chi)$, the Weil-morphism condition [def-wf-weil-category]. Multiplying on the left by $\chi^{-1}$ and on the right by $H(\chi^{-1})$ gives $\alpha H(\chi^{-1})=\chi^{-1}\delta$, since $H(\chi)H(\chi^{-1})=1$. Thus the inverse is also a Weil morphism, and both composites are identities by Step 1.

source.place: Penultimate sentence, equivariance for Weil complexes; argument extracted from lem-wf-tensor-completion-frobenius, original step 5; raw rationalization and common-stage Weil morphisms

proof.text: For inputs at $E,F$ and the specified common field $L$, apply the transition functors of [def-wf-weil-category] to obtain two Weil pairs at $L$, then apply Steps 1–5 there. Represent the tensor objects at $L$. The common-stage composition rule gives $[L,\chi^{-1}][L,\chi]=[L,1]$ and $[L,\chi][L,\chi^{-1}]=[L,1]$, hence inverse common-stage morphisms. If $L=E=F$, use the same rule and the prescribed identity-stage identifications. Nothing here compares components calculated at distinct fields.
